title: Make it negative
subtitle: How to form negative sentences: ne... pas, jamais, plus, rien, personne, aucun, que, ni... ni... in every tense and structure

tags.etre: after être: pas un, pas du
tags.subject: personne ne, rien ne

why.ne-pas: Ne goes before the conjugated verb (n' before a vowel) and pas after it.
why.pas-de: After a negation un, une, du, de la, des become de (d' before a vowel).
why.etre: After être the article does not change: ce n'est pas un livre, ce n'est pas du chocolat.
why.jamais: Ne goes before the verb and jamais after it. In the passé composé: ne + avoir + jamais + participle.
why.plus: Ne... plus means no longer, not any more. Du, de la, des become de: plus de pain.
why.rien: Ne goes before the verb, rien after it. In the passé composé rien comes before the participle: je n'ai rien vu.
why.personne: Personne comes after the participle in the passé composé: je n'ai vu personne.
why.pas-encore: Pas encore means not yet. In the passé composé: je n'ai pas encore fini.
why.pas-du-tout: Ne... pas du tout means not at all; du tout comes after pas.
why.subject: Personne and rien can be the subject: they go first, and ne stays before the verb. There is no pas.
why.aucun: Aucun and aucune mean none. They agree with the noun and are used in the singular. There is no pas.
why.que: Ne... que means only. Ne goes before the verb, que right before the word it limits. The article does not change.
why.ni-ni: Ne goes before the verb, and each ni comes before one of the two items. There is no pas and usually no article.
why.nulle-part: Nulle part is the negative of quelque part and partout. In the passé composé it goes after the participle.
why.combined: Negative words can be combined: jamais rien, jamais personne, plus rien, plus jamais, plus personne. There is only one ne.
why.compound: In the passé composé ne goes before avoir or être and pas goes after it, before the participle.
why.modal: With two verbs the negation goes around the first one: je ne vais pas venir, il ne peut pas venir.
why.tenses: In every tense ne goes before the conjugated verb and pas after it. In the passé composé it goes around the auxiliary.
why.imperative: In the negative command ne goes before the verb and pas after it; pronouns stay before the verb: ne me regarde pas.
why.reflexive: The reflexive pronoun stays right before the verb: ne goes before it. Je ne me lève pas.
why.infinitive: With a negative infinitive both parts stand together before the verb: ne pas partir, ne rien dire, ne jamais mentir.
why.pronouns: Ne goes before the pronouns and pas after the verb: je ne le vois pas. In the passé composé: je ne l'ai pas vu.
why.reverse: Take the negative words away and bring the articles back: pas de viande becomes de la viande.
why.spoken: In everyday speech the ne is often dropped, but you need it in writing and in formal French.
